title: Cost-Constrained Label Audits for ATE Estimation with Two Weakly Reliable Codes
banked_reason: Validity-confirmed terminal:proposal-no-pass at field floor; six reviewed versions over two angles retain letter-tier N-no-stat-frontier-advance; no D0 or Lean proof completed.
gap_reasons: The matched rate is confined to a self-created three-parameter triangular weak-channel family and is neither a strict improvement over a named published bound nor a first bound for a named existing method or new estimand; as the core itself states, this supports at most subfield/letter positioning, below novelty_target=field.
Any result is conditional on this sensitivity family; those restrictions cap the present positioning below field unless a transfer to a published broader class is added.
Revise toward a shared broader validation class and a named comparator separation; otherwise retain this as a letter/subfield benchmark rather than advancing it at the field novelty floor.
proof_attempt_summary: Six proposal versions across two angles attempted crossed-audit global risk gain, exact critical decision geometry, a matched audit-growth minimax frontier, and cost-constrained unequal allocation. Source verification and operational allocation repairs resolved distinct review findings, but all results stayed inside a bespoke balanced binary weak-channel family below the field novelty floor. The run stopped before D0; every substantive theorem remains an unproved obligation, with no Lean output or axiom-clean proof claimed.
tldr: Cost-constrained disjoint single-label audits have a sharp consistency boundary when both clinical-code reliabilities scale as \(n^{-1/4}\). For budget \(B_n=\lfloor Cn^\alpha\rfloor\), uniform causal ATE consistency holds exactly when \(\alpha>1/2\). Above the boundary, the all-procedure squared risk is asymptotic to \(\mathcal V(\lambda)\sqrt n/B_n\), attained by a total protected count estimator using crossed associations and calibration moments. The worst local precision occurs at the lower strength endpoints and \(|\theta|=1/2\). A strictly concave one-dimensional information criterion determines the cost-optimal review share, exact conditions for equal disjoint counts to be optimal, and a positive constant loss when those conditions fail. Below the boundary the experiment reduces to the bulk score; at the boundary the unequal five-coordinate Gaussian saddle and calibration use remain explicit open problems requiring whole-box verification. The allocation rule is a prospective sensitivity-class planning rule, with no empirical weak-code claim.
gap: Regular validation-design optimization and paired-label causal efficiency theory do not determine this disjoint dual-weak all-procedure cost frontier. The unresolved comparison is among legal cost allocations within the prescribed causal family.
fill: Five sufficient binomials connect the audit budget to information. Original-binomial local lower bounds and protected sharp attainment justify the maximin allocation criterion. Its unique solution and equal-allocation equality locus yield an operational treatment-only versus outcome-only review split. Critical endpoint support and calibration dependence are resolved separately, then transferred to counts.
